subject: Order form — invoicing cadence, minimum commit phasing, and tax residency
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudmesh.io, marco.bianchi@cloudmesh.io
Date: 2025-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Order Form — invoicing, min-commit and taxes

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sending over the draft Order Form last week. Finance has a few clarifying questions before we proceed to redlines:

- We need to confirm the invoicing cadence for the annual minimum commit (is it upfront or phased across the year?).
- Can Redwood invoice our EU entity (CloudMesh Srl) or do you require invoicing to Redwood US? We need to understand where VAT will be handled.
- Net terms: our standard is Net45 — would Redwood consider Net45 instead of Net30?
- We will provide tax residency and VAT registration certificates, but please confirm the required format and if you need a signed form.

We are fairly happy with the pricing schedule but we may ask for a 10% ramp on the minimum commit over the first two quarters. Attaching a short PO intent (stub) 

Appreciate a quick reply; legal asked for an expected timeline to circulate redlines.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement, CloudMesh
elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io

Attachments: CloudMesh_PO_intent_stub.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Order Form — invoicing, min-commit and taxes

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Answers / proposals:
- Invoicing cadence: we can support either (a) full upfront invoice for the annual minimum commit, (b) phased invoicing (equal quarterly invoices) or (c) staged ramp where the first invoice covers an initial tranche and subsequent invoices are triggered on quarters. For commercial flexibility I propose option (b) by default and (c) if you want the 10% ramp you mentioned.
- Invoicing entity: Redwood typically invoices Redwood Inc. (US) by default, but we can invoice Redwood EU branch for EU-resident customers to simplify VAT flow. If you want Redwood to invoice CloudMesh Srl directly, we need to confirm the counterparty details and tax forms.
- Net terms: standard offering is Net30; I flagged Net45 as a negotiable commercial term. Ben, can we accommodate Net45 for CloudMesh given DEAL-9876 scale?
- Tax evidence: please send VAT registration and a signed tax residency certificate (pdf). Kimberly — can you confirm required language and whether we need any additional forms for EU invoicing?

Attached: CloudMesh_OrderForm_Draft_v2.docx (draft with pricing schedule and proposed phasing).

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm invoicing entity preference and PO intent (Elena)
- Tomorrow: internal legal to provide redline guidance (Kimberly)
- Fri 10/24: finalize order form and share for signature / DocuSign

If that works I will circulate a one-page summary (MAP) for procurement.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

Attachment: CloudMesh_OrderForm_Draft_v2.docx (attachment stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-22T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Order Form — invoicing, min-commit and taxes

Elena — quick commercial note from our side. Thanks for the PO intent. A couple of practical options so procurement can pick one:

Option A (default, simplest):
- Annual minimum commit invoiced upfront at signing
- Net30
- Redwood invoices Redwood Inc. (US), CloudMesh handles VAT per reverse-charge where applicable

Option B (staggered, preferred for cash flow):
- Annual minimum commit split into 4 equal invoices (quarterly)
- 10% ramp: Q1 = 40% of annual min, Q2 = 30%, Q3 = 20%, Q4 = 10%
- Net45 (exception) allowed for this deal if CloudMesh can accept a $200k early-payment holdback for the first quarter
- Redwood can invoice Redwood EU entity to simplify VAT (requires your EU billing entity details)

I recommend Option B given your ask — we are flexible on Net45 if accounting accepts the early-payment holdback.

Pricing excerpt (from the draft):
- Annual min commit: EUR 1,200,000
- Effective blended rate: $0.0009/token (volume discount tiers in Order Form)
- Activation fee: EUR 25,000 (one-time, prorated if phased)

Hannah / Kimberly — please note the holdback request and legal redlines on invoicing entity and PO-to-invoice matching.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io>
Date: 2025-10-23T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Order Form — invoicing, min-commit and taxes

Team / Elena — I reviewed the draft Order Form and flagged the following items in the redline (Drive link below):

Redline highlights:
- Invoicing entity clause: allow Redwood EU branch (Redwood Ireland Ltd) as invoicing party if customer provides EU entity details and VAT ID. If CloudMesh wants Redwood to invoice CloudMesh Srl directly, we require counterparty legal name, VAT ID and PO contact.
- Net terms: Net30 is standard. We can accept Net45 as a commercial concession for this deal, conditional on: (i) signed amendment in Order Form, (ii) a $200k holdback or payment tranche as Ben suggested, or (iii) an early-pay discount to offset credit risk.
- Taxes: include explicit reverse-charge language for B2B EU customers and require VAT registration evidence on file prior to first invoice.
- Minimum commit phasing: add language for invoicing triggers and failure to meet tranche payments (proration / termination rights).
- PO matching: require PO number on invoice for accounting to accept payment; include an appendix specifying invoice recipient and remittance details per entity.

Drive (redline): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/CloudMesh-OF-v2
DocuSign envelope prepared (placeholder id): DocuSign:0x8a3f-CloudMesh-OF

Elena — please confirm you can provide CloudMesh Srl VAT certificate and a signed tax residency pdf. Also confirm which of Ben's options (A vs B) you prefer so we can lock the language.

I can turn around a clean redline today; Hannah, happy for you to send final to procurement after I merge changes.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmesh.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-24T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Order Form — invoicing, min-commit and taxes

Thanks all — quick update from procurement / finance at CloudMesh: we are comfortable with Option B (staggered with 10% ramp) and can accept Net45. We will provide:

- Signed tax residency certificate (pdf) and VAT registration for CloudMesh Srl (attached stub).
- Formal PO to be issued within 48 hours referencing the final Order Form ID (please confirm exact invoice recipient entity and remittance address to put on the PO).

A couple of asks before we sign: please add the holdback clause language that Ben mentioned (amount and release cadence), and include explicit reverse-charge text for EU VAT. We are okay with Redwood invoicing Redwood Ireland Ltd if that simplifies remittance; just confirm the invoice recipient details for our AP team.

If you can send the merged redline and final clean Order Form + DocuSign link, we'll route for signature.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement, CloudMesh

Attachments: Tax_Certificates_CloudMesh.pdf (attachment stub)
